blocks.text: St. Canice is associated principally with Aghaboe in what is now County Laois. His names appear in English as Canice, Cainnech and Kenneth. The historical reference cautions that his ancestry and early movements are difficult to reconstruct from the surviving traditions.

blocks.text: His medieval Life describes study, priestly ministry, periods of solitary prayer and the foundation of churches. It makes Aghaboe his principal community. Other early material associates him with St. Columba of Iona and places connected with Ireland and Scotland. These accounts explain his wide commemoration, while their later composition limits how precisely his travels can be reconstructed.

blocks.text: The sources give differing years, 600 and 603, for his death. They commemorate him on October 11. This profile therefore retains an approximate chronology and does not invent a manner of death or classify him as a martyr.
